_comment: Recorded verdicts for findings scripts/check-secret-resolver-drift.py
would otherwise report, in the same 'annotated entry with a reason'
shape scripts/pub-item-verdicts.json uses for scan-pub-item-usage.py.
This is not a bare allowlist of paths: every entry needs a non-empty
'reason', and the checker refuses to run (exit 2) without one.
Keys are '<repo-relative file>::<function name>::<shape>', where
<shape> is 'adhoc-parse' (shape 1: a hand-rolled env:/file:/provider-URI
scheme match outside crates/sbproxy-vault/src/) or
'passthrough-fallback' (shape 2: a secret-shaped function whose
guardless fallback hands a parameter back unchanged). The checker fails
if a key names a finding that no longer exists, so this file cannot
rot into a list of excuses for code that was already fixed.
Most entries below are 'reviewed': a real, already-audited call site
that is either the resolver's own public entry point or a documented
fallback for when no resolver is installed (env:/file: only; a
provider URI is refused rather than becoming the secret). One entry,
billing's provider_label_for_key, is 'false-positive': its `key` is a
payment idempotency key, not a config secret reference.
A third verdict, 'escalated', is for a finding that is real and not
yet fixed. There is none right now: the one entry that carried it,
signatures.rs::decode_secret, was fixed by WOR-2301, which routed
message_signatures.key through the resolver and removed the entry.

crates/sbproxy-core/src/config_source.rs.reason: This IS the shared entry point for source: / config-authority secret references (WOR-1767/WOR-2282): it routes through sbproxy_vault::process_resolver() when one is installed, and its env:/file: handling here is the documented fallback for sbproxy validate / unit tests / a config with no proxy.secrets backends, where a provider URI is refused outright rather than resolved.

crates/sbproxy-core/src/key_plane.rs::re.reason: Delegates to sbproxy_vault::process_resolver() first (WOR-2285); the local env:/file: handling is the documented no-resolver-installed fallback for key_management.crypto material, and a provider URI without an installed resolver is refused via looks_like_secret_reference_uri rather than becoming the key (this is the exact WOR-1767/pepper incident the function's own doc comment cites).

crates/sbproxy-core/src/pipeline.rs::res.reason: Same shape as key_plane::resolve_secret_material: resolves through sbproxy_vault::process_resolver() first, and the local file: handling is the documented no-resolver-installed fallback for at-rest encryption key material. A provider URI without a resolver is refused via looks_like_secret_reference_uri before the literal-bytes fallback, per its own doc comment.

crates/sbproxy-core/src/cluster.rs::reso.reason: Resolves the cluster shared-key reference through sbproxy_vault::process_resolver() first (WOR-2285); the local env:/file: handling is the documented no-resolver-installed fallback, and every provider-URI scheme (not just vault://) is refused via looks_like_secret_reference_uri before falling through, per the WOR-2064-era incident documented at the call site.

crates/sbproxy-core/src/server/action_di.reason: Delegates to sbproxy_vault::process_resolver() when installed; the local env: handling is the documented no-resolver fallback, and the function's own doc comment records the deliberate third case (a bare, unprefixed variable name) this call site has always accepted as env: shorthand.

The companion shape-guard for mcp_secret_lookup: decides whether a credential_ref carries none of the resolver's recognized forms (env:, file:, ${VAR}, or a provider-URI scheme), so it is a bare variable name rather than something the resolver would mis-resolve or reject. Documented at the definition; not a resolver reimplementation, a classifier for the one deliberately-scoped bare-name case.

crates/sbproxy-config/src/cluster.rs::va.reason: Validate-time (not resolve-time) shape check for security.shared_key, consistent with the runtime check in sbproxy-core's cluster::resolve_secret_material (WOR-2285): env:/file: are accepted as references to inject at runtime, and crate::types::is_secret_reference (the shared shape guard, reused rather than a hardcoded scheme allowlist) refuses every provider-URI scheme rather than just vault://, per the WOR-2064-era incident documented at the definition.

crates/sbproxy-modules/src/auth/dpop_out.reason: Validate-time shape check for a DPoP signing key reference, the same shape as sbproxy-config::cluster::validate_shared_key_reference: file: is accepted directly (the resolver has no bare guard for that form), and every other reference shape is delegated to sbproxy_vault::looks_like_secret_reference_uri rather than hand-matched. HTTP URLs and inline PEM are refused by the same check.

crates/sbproxy/src/main.rs::is_secret_re.reason: A display-time masking guard for `sbproxy plan`/doctor output (WOR-1869): decides whether a config string is a resolver reference (safe to print) or inline material (must be masked), never resolves anything. It duplicates the shape check sbproxy_config::types::is_secret_reference already performs because that one is pub(crate) and unreachable from the sbproxy binary crate; wiring the two together is a real cleanup but a separate, non-security-bearing change from this ticket's scope.

crates/sbproxy-billing/src/types.rs::pro.reason: `key` here is a payment-provider idempotency key for a rail's dedup label, not a config secret reference; `key.to_string()` in `Ok(key.to_string())` is the ordinary short-key case of a label-shortening helper, unrelated to sbproxy-vault. Flagged only because the function/parameter name matches the shape-2 term filter ("key"), which this checker's own docstring says is expected to happen for the generic terms it uses.

crates/sbproxy-extension/src/bundle/enve.reason: Delegates to sbproxy_vault::process_resolver() first (WOR-2289); the local ${VAR}/file: handling is the documented no-resolver-installed fallback for bundle secret_vars, and a reference nothing can resolve returns an Err naming proxy.secrets.backends rather than passing the reference through as the secret. Same reviewed shape as config_source::resolve_secret_reference. Needed because #951 added this function one commit before #952 added this checker, so the checker's original exemption set never saw it.
